correctness.rationale: Pinned RESULT.md uses the exact rank-n orthogonal kernel K(x,y)=Σ(x_i-p_i)(y_i-p_i)/(p_i(1-p_i)); on finite C(Ω), norm is max_x E|K(x,Y)|, attained by choosing input sign of that row. At x_i rare, the individual centered summand U has endpoints -1 and (1-r)/r; at common x_i, V has endpoints -1 and r/(1-r) contained in [minU,maxU]; both have zero mean. Chord convexity proves V≤cx U, and independence lets one replace each common coordinate for convex |S+t|, yielding global rare-corner optimum for arbitrary heterogeneous p_i. At homogeneous p the row is ±(Bin(n,p)-np)/min(p,1-p); binomial telescoping yields 2n max(p,q) C(n-1,floor(np)) p^{floor(np)} q^{n-1-floor(np)}. Local CLT and Poisson convergence prove fixed-bias sqrt n and sparse p=c/n linear boundary; integer c handled by equal adjacent Poisson masses. Independently exact-rational enumerated 308 row assertions including four heterogeneous profiles and homogeneous n≤5. Boundaries n=1, p=1/2 included.
